sentences.text:
Accused No.1 in Crime No.89/2023 registered by Hanumanthanagar Police Station, Bangalore City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (hereinafter referred to as 'IPC' for short) and under Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 (hereinafter referred to as 'DP Act' for short) is before this Court seeking anticipatory bail.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
3.

On the basis of complaint lodged by one Aishwary C. wife of the petitioner herein on 19.05.2023,
Hanumanthanagar Police Station, Bengaluru City has registered FIR in Crime No.89/2023 against the petitioner and three others for the aforesaid offences.

In the complaint it is stated that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with the petitioner on 27.03.2022 and it NC:
2023:KHC:28554 was in arranged marriage.
It is further stated in the complaint that the marriage had not consummated because the petitioner was not in position to perform sexual activities.
In this regard it appears that there was a misunderstanding between the parties.
It is alleged that during her stay in her matrimonial house, the petitioner and his family members have tortured her for dowry and also outraged her modesty.

Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed an application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. before the Court of LXXI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-74) in Crl.Misc. No.4684/2023, which was dismissed as against him.

entities.text: LXXI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner reiterating the grounds urged in the petition submits that petitioner is innocent of the alleged offences and a false complaint has been foisted against him.
He further submits that considering the nature of allegations made in the NC: 2023:KHC:28554 complaint, this Court has granted interim bail to him subject to conditions on 11.07.2023.
He submits that the petitioner has co-operated with the Investigating Officer and major portion of the investigation is already completed.

He further submits that accused Nos.2 to 4 as against whom,
identical allegations are made, have been released on bail.

He further submits that petitioner had Sri Pramod S vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81043987/
2 filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for restitution of conjugal rights in the month of April 2023 and in the said petition, it is clearly stated that the complainant had left the matrimonial house in the month of August - 2022 itself.

entities.text: Sri Pramod S vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complaint is lodged after filing of the petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which is a counter to the petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the de-facto complainant submits that serious charges of assault and torture are made in the complaint.
The NC: 2023:KHC:28554 accused persons have also outraged the modesty of the complainant.
Petitioner has not complied with the terms of the interim bail granted by this Court.
He has not handed over the marks card of the complainant.

She further submits that the summons in the petition filed under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 was received by the complainant only after filing of criminal complaint against the accused persons.
Therefore, she prays to dismiss the petition.

6. Learned HCGP on instruction from the Investigating Officer, who is present before the Court submits that the petitioner has co-operated with the Investigating Officer for the purpose of investigation and a mahazar was also drawn in his house and all the articles belonging to complainant have been handed over by the petitioner.
She further submits that there were no other articles belonging to the complainant found in the house of the petitioner.

From a perusal of the complaint averments itself it is seen that the relationship between the wife and husband got strained immediately after the marriage since the petitioner who was not in a position to consummate the marriage.
The complaint averments disclose that the couple had fought against each other on this issue.
The nature of allegations made in the complaint with regard to subsequent events looks abnormal.

Serious allegations have been made against accused Nos.2 to 4,
more particularly against accused No.3.

Accused Nos.2 to 4 have been granted anticipatory bail by the Court of LXXI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-72) in Crl.Misc.
No.4684/2023 on 02.06.2023.
8.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Taking into consideration, the nature of allegations made in the petition and also considering the fact that the case registered against the petitioner was for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Section 3 and 4 of the DP Act, the co-ordinate bench of this Court had granted an NC: 2023:KHC:28554 interim bail to the petitioner on 11.07.2023, subject to certain conditions.

9. Learned HCGP on instructions from the Investigating Officer, who is present before the Court,
has submitted that the petitioner has co-operated with the Investigating Officer and the belongings of the complainant which were available with him in his house have been handed over to the Investigating Officer and a mahazar was also accordingly drawn.
She has also submitted that the conditions imposed by this Court while granting interim bail to the petitioner has been complied by the petitioner.

Petitioner has been arraigned as an accused in a criminal case registered for offence punishable under Sections 498A, 354 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of the Sri Pramod S vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81043987/
3 DP Act.

sentences.text: The maximum punishment provided for these offences is up to five years and the offences are triable by the Court of Magistrate.

Learned HCGP on instructions has submitted that the petitioner has co-operated with the investigating NC: 2023:KHC:28554 Officer for the purpose of investigation and major portion of the investigation is completed.
Under these circumstances, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has made out prima facie case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other Police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.89/2023 registered by Hanumanthanagar Police Station, Bangalore City for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 354 read with Section 34 of IPC and under Section 3 and 4 of the DP Act, subject to the following conditions:
1. Petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000 (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer.
Petitioner shall regularly appear before the trial Court without fail unless exempted by the trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the Police for investigation and appear before the Investigating Officer whenever called upon.
